svg.aria-label: Raising and transplanting seedlings: 1 seedling soil: 6 parts garden soil that has not grown nightshades or cucurbits for 3 years plus 4 parts fully rotted compost or farmyard manure, sieved, with a little wood ash if wanted; sterilise by spreading it thinly in hot sun for a few days or steaming it for about half an hour; containers need drainage holes in the bottom, or the soil can be cut into 8-10 cm blocks. 2 Stir fruiting-vegetable seed constantly in water at about 55°C for 15 minutes, then soak in water at room temperature (fruiting vegetables 8-12 hours, cucurbits 4-6 hours), wrap in a damp cloth and keep at 25-30°C to pre-germinate, rinse in warm water once a day, and sow when most seeds show a white tip. 3 Water thoroughly first, scatter the seed once the water has soaked in, cover with sieved fine soil to about 2-3 times the seed's diameter (fruiting vegetables 0.5-1 cm), cover with plastic to keep moist, and uncover as soon as the seedlings appear. 4 Fruiting vegetables 25-30°C before emergence, after emergence 20-25°C by day and 12-15°C at night; nights too warm or too little light make seedlings leggy; let the soil dry, then water, in the morning; prick out at 2-3 true leaves. 5 Start hardening off 7-10 days before planting out, putting seedlings outside by day in a sheltered, half-shaded spot, at first for a few hours and a little longer each day. 6 Transplant on an overcast day or after 3 or 4 p.m. on a sunny one, with a root ball, water in with about 0.5-1 L per plant, settling in takes 3-5 days. Planting depth: tomatoes can be planted deep; peppers and cucumbers level with or slightly below the old soil line; do not bury the heart of lettuce or Chinese cabbage
